text:
Mia Chen: Rolling out SDK v12.0.0 now — minor streaming change that reintroduced `ledger_cursor` in the stream payload (supposed to be deprecated). Canaries green locally but noticing a spike in errors from the to-prod canary group. :rotating_light:
DeployBot: rollout started for sdk/v12.0.0 at 2026-03-15T10:01:40Z (canary cohort = 5% traffic).
Oncall Bot: paging-errors service:rate > 5% for 3m in prod-canary (rule: paging.stream.client_errors).
Raj Patel: seeing a lot of client-side 400s from partners using legacy paging. They treat `ledger_cursor` as authoritative; when present it forces an offset reset.
Sam O'Neill: logs look like: ``ERROR streaming: invalid cursor before offset 0; payload: {client_id: "acme", ledger_cursor: "0xdeadbeef"} ``. Some clients then request pages that don't exist and we return 404, cascade back to app.
Mia Chen: removing the field from payload is quick, but need coordination — canary still in flight. Options: 1) feature flag kill-switch to stop sending ledger_cursor, 2) rollback the SDK rollout, 3) quick server-side tolerance shim to ignore ledger_cursor. Thoughts?
Tanya Lopez: we should kill the flag first (least blast). If that isn't fast, rollback. Notify CS for impacted customers.
Kevin Wu: oncall here — I can flip the kill-flag in config-db. Command: ``PATCH /flags/sdk_streaming_v12_ledger_cursor {"value": false}``
Mia Chen: do it. Post the request/response and ETA.
Kevin Wu: PATCH sent. Response: 200 OK. Flag propagation to edge in ~45s. :white_check_mark:
Oncall Bot: feature-flag sdk_streaming_v12_ledger_cursor toggled OFF by Kevin Wu at 2026-03-15T10:03:12Z.
Raj Patel: seeing error rate drop in canary already. Good signal.
DeployBot: canary traffic snapshot: errors reduced from 6.3% -> 0.8% within 90s.
Sam O'Neill: still a handful of stuck clients that received the field earlier — they need session reset. Forwarding to CS to advise a client restart or fallback.
Mia Chen: customer-impact estimate: ~12 partner integrations received bad pages in 5% canary window; two reported partial outages (internal logs show retries and backoffs). No large-scale user-facing outages yet.
Incident Triage: classifying as Sev2 for now until we confirm no data loss and rollback status. Assigning owner for mitigation and comms.
Tanya Lopez: I'll take owner for mitigation. I'm on the TSV: contacting top 10 partners via CS now.
Mia Chen: next steps: 1) keep flag off, 2) stop rollout (abort remaining canaries), 3) prepare rollback artifact for v11 pin if needed, 4) postmortem and SDK release gating rules.
DeployBot: remaining canary batches halted by automated kill-switch at 2026-03-15T10:05:00Z.
Kevin Wu: double-checking server shim option — we can add server-side ignore logic to treat unknown `ledger_cursor` values as a soft field for a 48-hour window. That requires a small runtime patch; I'd prefer the shim as short-term if customers can't restart.
Raj Patel: shim is a code change in runtime parsing: ``if payload.ledger_cursor && !client_supports_ledger: ignore``. Low-risk but needs deploy; team ETA ~2 hours.
Mia Chen: for now keep flag off and do not roll forward. Tanya, coordinate CS comms: message to affected partners with recommended client restart and ETA for fix. Add note that we're not rolling back globally yet.
Tanya Lopez: drafting message. Will include suggested steps and link to status page.
Sam O'Neill: adding observability tasks: create synthetic checks for legacy paging clients to ensure no regressions when we flip back.
Mia Chen: handoff: Kevin stays primary on mitigation patch; Raj will own telemetry and logs; Tanya owns CS comms; Sam will validate checks and run canary once fixed.
Incident Triage: Handoff recorded — primary: Kevin Wu, secondary: Mia Chen. Oncall shift change at 2026-03-15T12:00Z will be notified.
Tanya Lopez: CS message sent to 12 partners at 10:12Z — 3 responded immediately asking for a rollback instead of client restart.
Mia Chen: prepare rollback plan in case flag flip insufficient. Command reference: ``/rollback-sdk v12 --to v11 --reason "ledger_cursor compatibility"``. Who can execute?
Kevin Wu: I can execute rollback if we need to. But avoid unless necessary. We'll wait 30m and confirm error floor.
DeployBot: canary error floor stable at ~0.7% after flag off. Trend shows decline.
Raj Patel: will collect post-fix logs for duplicate/404 occurrences and prepare impact summary: count of failed pages, distinct partners, last seen offsets. ETA 30m.
Sam O'Neill: creating post-incident ticket and linking telemetry dashboards.
Mia Chen: good. If any partner reports ongoing outage, escalate and trigger rollback. Otherwise we'll schedule a quick runtime shim deploy target ~+2h and a follow-up for a formal postmortem.
Oncall Bot: reminder — notify morning oncall at handoff with summary: flag off, rollback on standby, impacted partners = 12 (2 partial), Sev2.
Tanya Lopez: logged a follow-up that CS will send a staged customer update at 11:00Z.
Kevin Wu: starting prep for shim branch now. Sharing patch PR number when ready.
Mia Chen: thanks team. Keep messages short in this thread so the morning oncall can read a concise timeline. 
Tanya Lopez: adding brief timeline to the incident doc. :memo:
Sam O'Neill: noted — I'll add the canary metrics and link to synthetic checks.
Mia Chen: final for now — flag left off, canary halted, rollback on standby. Handoff to next oncall at 12:00Z.
Incident Triage: thread closed for active updates; reopen if severity changes. :lock:
